finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test makes a server-side POST to an arbitrary URL from the request body, with no validation. Only the target's status code is returned, so the attacker gets a blind SSRF and a status-code oracle for internal hosts.
finding.source: req.body.callback, from the body of pub.post('/hooks/test') (routes.js:19-20)

trace.note: Route is on the 'pub' router, which has no auth middleware in this file
req.body.callback is passed unchanged as the axios URL argument
Only r.status is returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: None in this file: no scheme allowlist, no host/IP denylist or allowlist, no DNS pinning, no port restriction, no authentication. axios follows redirects by default, so a redirect would bypass any initial check. Assumption: the parent app does not put authentication in front of the 'pub' router. That app is not in this directory. If it does, severity drops to authenticated-user SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-21 has no validation, allowlist, or auth on the pub.post('/hooks/test') handler. The only auth is requireAdmin at routes.js:7-12, which is applied to the admin router, not pub. No parent app is in this directory, so middleware mounted above pub cannot be checked.
verdict.reason: All trace lines are accurate (routes.js:19 pub.post, routes.js:20 axios.post(req.body.callback), routes.js:21 returns only r.status) and no guard exists in routes.js, but whether an unauthenticated remote attacker can reach pub at routes.js:19 depends on how the parent app mounts the router, and that code is not in this directory.

finding.claim: Admin-only GET /diagnostics/fetch fetches an arbitrary URL from req.query.url with no validation. Only the status code is returned, so it is blind. The route is gated by requireAdmin, so severity is lower, but it is still an SSRF primitive that can reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: req.query.url, from the query string of admin.get('/diagnostics/fetch') (routes.js:14)

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies to every route on the admin router
req.query.url is passed unchanged as the axios URL argument
Only r.status is returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check only (routes.js:7-9). No URL validation of any kind. axios follows redirects by default. Because the caller is an admin, this is a privilege-boundary issue, not an unauthenticated one. Its impact depends on how many people hold the admin role.

verdict.guard_found: No URL validation exists at routes.js:14-16. The only guard is the admin session check: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied to the whole router by admin.use at routes.js:12) returns 403 unless req.session.role === 'admin'.
verdict.reason: All trace lines match the code (routes.js:7, 12, 15, 16), but the source fails the attacker-control check: req.query.url at routes.js:15 is only reachable after requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, 12) confirms an admin session, so the value is admin-controlled, not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege remote attacker. The finding is a privileged-user SSRF concern, not a CONFIRMED finding under the stated criteria.
